title: Hosting a Client-Rendered Application knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Hosting a Client-Rendered Application”?
options: Hosting a Client-Rendered Application helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Hosting a Client-Rendered Application means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Hosting a Client-Rendered Application removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Hosting a Client-Rendered Application should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Hosting a Client-Rendered Application helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Hosting a Client-Rendered Application is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Static hosting fundamentals” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Static hosting fundamentals” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Static hosting fundamentals” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Static hosting fundamentals” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Static hosting fundamentals” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Static hosting fundamentals” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Static hosting fundamentals” under Hosting a Client-Rendered Application. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Hosting a Client-Rendered Application”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
